thread.title: Forget Facebook and Apple and buy cheap BANG stocks

author: Barbara Kollmeyer
title: Forget Facebook and Apple and buy cheap BANG stocks
text:
Published: Oct 5, 2018 9:31 a.m. ET Share
Critical information for the U.S. trading day Getty Images Chancing on a beat down sector
By Markets reporter
Get ready to hit the ground running.
We hit the mother lode on Friday—jobs data, bond-yield watching, White House/China friction, plus a vote that begins on a hot-button Supreme court nominee.
If that’s not enough, there’s ongoing fallout from a Bloomberg report that said China planted teeny tiny spy chips in U.S. computers doesn’t look to be over. Big tech names like Apple AAPL, -1.77% came under pressure, weighing on the Nasdaq COMP, -1.17% on Thursday, with that sector also hurting in Asia Friday (see Chart of the Day). See Also Feinstein: White House May Have Blocked FBI From Doing Its Job ×
The pain for investors could spread further. Apple is a top holding in the SPDR S&P 500 ETF SPY, -0.60% —a big proxy for the S&P 500—and such passive-investing vehicles have become extremely popular in this yearslong bull market.
That brings us to our call of the day from The Felder Report’s Jesse Felder, who suggests going against the crowd with some cheap, anti-passive precious metals miners.
“It looks to me like they have been left for dead and, for this reason, present a terrific opportunity for true value investors, regardless of the bullish case for gold. And if the gold price takes off, today’s BANG share prices will certainly look like an unbelievable bargain in retrospect,” said Felder, in a blog post.
Felder says the so-called BANG (Barrick Gold ABX, -1.63% ABX, -1.26% Agnico Eagle AEM, +0.30% Newmont Mining NEM, +0.71% and Goldcorp GG, -2.11% G, -1.44% ) stocks are trading at their cheapest in decades. Meanwhile, the FANG highfliers (Facebook FB, -0.94% Amazon AMZN, -1.07% Netflix NFLX, -3.47% and Alphabet’s Google GOOGL, -0.86% ) are hitting their highest valuations in history, he notes.
He attributes this to the fact that big tech names dominate ETFs, while mining stocks are far less represented in those passive funds. That‘s laid out in his chart below (Note: Newmont Mining pops up, but in ETFs with hardly any assets, he says): Tech domination
“Conversely, the lack of interest in the BANG stocks is indicative of the fear investors have of the group after a massive bear market. Those wishing to heed the famous words of Warren Buffett should thus be fearful of the FANG stocks and greedy in the BANG stocks,” said Felder. The market
A mixed start is underway, post jobs data, with the S&P SPX, -0.60% ,Nasdaq COMP, -1.17% and Dow DJIA, -0.74% are all modestly higher at the start.
The yield on the 10-year Treasury note TMUBMUSD10Y, +1.64% is hovering at 2011 highs. Crude US:CLU8 is up, while gold US:GCU8 is modestly higher and the dollar DXY, -0.14% is holding steady.

Check out the Market Snapshot column for the latest action.
Europe stocks SXXP, -0.86% are sagging. while Taiwan’s Taiex Y9999, -1.88% led losses across Asia . China markets were closed. The economy
The September jobs report revealed a less-than-expected employment gain of 134,000, but the jobless rate dropped its lowest level in 49 years . The trade deficit jumped 6.4% to a six-month high . Consumer credit data is due later. The chart
In the wake of that Chinese spy chip report, laptop maker Lenovo 0992, -15.10% sold heavily in Hong Kong. Our chart of the day shows shares careening at the open, before closing down 15% on the day, even though the company tried to distance itself from the chip story . MarketWatch The difference a day makes for Lenovo
According to Statista , Lenovo ranked number 2 when it comes to market share of leading personal computer vendors across the globe in 2017, just behind HP HPQ, -4.14% The laptop maker also has a plant in North Carolina.
